content: Azelastine ophthalmic solution is prescribed to alleviate the itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis, commonly referred to as allergic pink eye. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as antihistamines. It functions by inhibiting the action of histamine, a chemical in the body responsible for triggering allergic symptoms. Azelastine is available as an eye drop formulation and is typically applied to the affected eye(s) twice daily. To ensure consistent use, it is recommended to administer the drops at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use azelastine exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of the medication or apply it more frequently than prescribed. To apply the eye drops, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 2. Use a mirror or have someone assist you in administering the drops. 3. Remove the protective cap from the bottle. Ensure the dropper tip is not chipped or cracked. 4. Avoid touching the dropper tip to your eye or any other surface to prevent contamination. 5. Always keep the dropper tip facing downward to prevent backflow of liquid into the bottle. 6. Lie down or tilt your head back. 7. Hold the bottle between your thumb and index finger, positioning the dropper as close to your eyelid as possible without touching it. 8. Use the remaining fingers of the same hand to brace against your cheek or nose for stability. 9. With the index finger of your other hand, gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pocket. 10. Administer the prescribed number of drops into the pocket formed by the lower eyelid. Avoid placing the drops directly on the surface of the eyeball, as this may cause stinging. 11. Close your eye and gently press against the lower eyelid with your finger for 2-3 minutes to retain the medication in the eye. Do not blink during this time. 12. Replace and tighten the cap immediately after use. Do not wipe or rinse the dropper tip. 13. Use a clean tissue to wipe away any excess liquid from your cheek. 14. Wash your hands again after application. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using azelastine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to azelastine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using azelastine, contact your doctor immediately. If your eyes are red, do not wear contact lenses. If your eyes are not red and you wear contact lenses, be aware that azelastine solution contains benzalkonium chloride, which can be absorbed by soft contact lenses. Remove your contact lenses before applying azelastine and wait at least 10 minutes before reinserting them. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Azelastine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: Eye burning or stinging Headaches Bitter taste Eye pain Blurred vision Excessive tiredness Sore throat In rare cases, azelastine may cause serious side effects. If you experience difficulty breathing, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while using this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
